security.heading: What the policies are
security.body: Chock adds friction. It is not a security boundary. A policy refuses a risky action, asks you about it, warns on it or flags it. It does not make the action impossible. An agent can ignore advisory text, and a determined agent can get around a block on the shell. Each policy's label says which of these it does.

security.heading: What the site does
security.body: The site is static files: nothing you pick leaves your machine, and the builder runs in your browser. Your selection lives in the URL fragment after the #, which browsers never send to a server. The author page saves a policy you draft only in this browser's localStorage. The page never sends it anywhere. Its share link holds the agent and catalog ids, and never your draft. There is no cookie and no account. The site counts a few actions and no page views, with no personal data. The list is at the end of this page.

security.heading: Why the command is safe to read before running
security.body: The command fetches one pinned catalog commit and checks every policy against its sha256. That is the same hash shown on the policy's page. If the pack does not match, the install fails and chock writes nothing. The commit must be on a branch or tag the catalog publishes, so a link cannot point at a fork's code.

security.heading: How to report a problem
security.body: Report it as a security issue in the chock-catalog repository. Do not open a public issue in the engine or site repositories.

install.install_note: You need Python 3.11 or newer. The engine is the only thing you install, and it builds the plugin from the pinned catalog.
install.run_body: Pick your agent and your policies on the builder, copy the command and run it in your repo. `--client` names the agent. For an agent marked tested, `--apply` also runs that agent's own install steps. For an untested agent, the command only builds the plugin, and you run the steps yourself.
install.update_body: Change your picks in the builder and re-run the command. Each agent's last step above says how it picks up a rebuild.
install.remove_body: Each agent's section above ends with its remove steps.
install.file_body: A selection is a small JSON or YAML file naming the agent, the pinned catalog commit and the policies you picked. The builder writes one for you. The install command reads the same file. These are the fields it checks:

file_fields.meaning: The agent the plugin is built for: __CLIENTS__. The --client option on the command line overrides it.
The plugin's version, __BUNDLE_VERSION__ from this site.
The pinned catalog commit. The plugin builds only from it.
Optional. A named catalog release over the commit.
Optional. The preset the picks started from.
One entry per picked policy: from (catalog), id, version and sha256.

warning_texts.file_absent: __PRESENT__ refuses everything until your repo has __FILE__. Create it before you install.

warning_texts.missing_partner:many: __PRESENT__ are picked without __ABSENT__. They cover one rule by different means, so pick them all.
warning_texts.file_absent:many: __PRESENT__ refuse everything until your repo has __FILE__. Create it before you install.
warning_texts.grade:advise:many: __PRESENT__ are text only: nothing stops a violation.
warning_texts.overlap: chock install warns when a picked policy is already in another chock plugin for the same agent: both copies would fire.

cursor.note: Delete the folder __PLUGIN_DIR__, then run "Developer: Reload Window".

codex.note: Uninstall __PLUGIN__ in /plugins, then delete the folder __PLUGIN_DIR__.

copilot.note: Uninstall __PLUGIN__ from the __MARKETPLACE__ marketplace in Copilot, then delete the folder __PLUGIN_DIR__.

devin.note: Remove __PLUGIN__ from Devin's plugins, then delete the folder __PLUGIN_DIR__.

goose.note: Delete the folder __PLUGIN_DIR__. Checked on Windows.
Optional tidy-up: delete the __PLUGIN__ entry in the plugins list of goose's config.yaml. goose works without this step.

grok.note: Run "grok plugin list" and find the name grok gave __PLUGIN__, run "grok plugin uninstall" with that name, then delete the folder __PLUGIN_DIR__.

antigravity.note: Close Antigravity, delete the folder ~/.gemini/config/plugins/__PLUGIN__, then reopen Antigravity. Checked on Windows.
Optional tidy-up: delete the build copy __PLUGIN_DIR__. Antigravity does not read it.
